newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: U.S. warns of terrorist threat to APEC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. warns of terrorist threat to APEC.

text.p: The United States on Friday warned Americans gathering for the Asia-Pacific summit they may be under threat of terrorist attack, and a secret Philippine intelligence report raised fears of bombings and assassinations.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns sounded an alarm for diplomats, journalists and others by saying they should take security precautions, but gave no details.

Philippine security sources said police had reported "strong indications" a leftist hit squad would launch terror attacks -- including bombings and assassinations -- to disrupt the summit, to be attended by U.S. President Bill Clinton, Chinese President Jiang Zemin and other key leaders.
An intelligence report obtained by Reuters meanwhile indicated that explosives found at Manila international airport on Wednesday night were not part of a drill as originally announced.
The report, for President Fidel Ramos, said a bomb comprising three grenades with their safety pins removed and held with tape had been found in a black bag on a stair in the arrivals area.
It said an airport security force was still investigating.

Officials at the time insisted the explosives had been placed there as part of a security drill. The same explanation had been given for a pipe bomb discovered a few hours earlier inside the gates of Subic Bay freeport where the summit is to take place.
The top secret, high-level Philippine police report on the overall terrorism threat did not name Americans as targets.

"There are strong indications that the ABB under the MRRPC will employ terrorism such as kidnappings, bombings and assassinations as their means of disrupting the summit," it said, according to the security sources.

The Alex Boncayao Brigade (ABB) is a leftist hit squad which specialises in attacking police and businessmen it considers corrupt or abusive. Police blame it for the murder of 200 police, soldiers and local officials in the late 1980s.

It had claimed responsibility for the killing in a Manila street ambush seven years ago of U.S. Army Colonel James Rowe, whom it accused of collaborating with Philippine security forces in combating leftist guerrilla groups.
Police say the ABB is the strike arm of the communist Metro Manila Rizal Regional Party Committee (MRRPC) under Filemon Lagman.
Lagman, chairman of a legitimate workers' group, was arrested two weeks ago on charges of murdering a policeman in 1992.

Leftist officials said security forces arrested activist Freddie Cunanan and his brother at their home north of Manila on Wednesday night. Cunanan was held on charges of illegal possession of ammunition and his brother of possessing subversive documents.

Satur Ocampo, spokesman for the People's Conference on Anti-Imperialist Globalisation, accused the government of a campaign of harassment to head off an anti-APEC motorcade due to leave for the Subic Bay summit site on Sunday.
"We will not be intimidated," he declared, predicting thousands would turn out for the protest.
The police report, written three weeks ago, said anti-APEC elements were at "full speed" to wreck the summit, according to the sources.
It said that as the summit itself, in the former U.S. naval base at Subic, 80 km (50 miles) from Manila, would be under tight security, the attackers might go for soft targets elsewhere.
"Another possibility is for them to victimise delegates and their staff when the latter are on touring sprees, visiting lightly secured tourist spots," the sources quoted it as saying.

Burns told reporters travelling with U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher the Philippine government had taken steps to assure the security of Americans as well as other delegates, but the United States felt compelled to alert the public.
Although the Philippine government has "responded in an excellent way to assure security... we feel it is incumbent upon us to warn you to take appropriate security measures," he said.
Summit preparations this week have been dogged by leftist protest unprecedented in APEC's seven years.
